add_block.new_heading: What is the cheapest way to cater an event in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Drop-off. It is the cheapest way to cater an event because you are paying for food and packaging and nothing else: no service staff, no equipment hire, no chef on site. Volume drop-off starts at AED 90 per person for a working or office lunch, with a 10-guest minimum and a minimum order value of AED 900. The next step up is a standard event buffet from AED 120 per person, which adds presentation and a small team to set it out and keep it stocked, and needs 20 guests. Premium buffet, BBQ, live stations and canapé receptions start at AED 150. Cheap event catering in Dubai goes wrong in the same three places every time, so it is worth naming them: a price quoted without VAT, a headcount minimum discovered after you commit, and staffing charged as an extra line once the venue turns out to need it. Every figure on this page carries 5% VAT on top and states its minimum, so you can compare it against anything else you have been sent.

Three things cut the bill without cutting the food. Serve fewer dishes in larger quantity — a six-item buffet done properly beats a twelve-item one spread thin, and it costs less. Move the event off a peak Friday or Saturday in the November-to-March window. And choose one format instead of layering three: passed canapés and a buffet and a dessert station is where budgets quietly double.

add_block.new_heading: Small event catering in Dubai — the minimums, stated plainly
new_paragraphs: Small event catering in Dubai has one question behind it: will anyone take the booking. The answer here is 10 guests for drop-off, platters and working-lunch formats, 20 guests for a buffet, and a minimum order value of AED 900 whichever you choose. A private chef cooking plated at your table carries no minimum headcount at all, which is why a dinner for six or eight is usually better served that way than by a scaled-down buffet — the food is cooked to order in the room, and nobody is maintaining a chafing dish for eight people. For a small party of twenty to forty, the format that works most often is a grazing table plus one live station: it fills the room visually, it needs a smaller team than plated service, and it gives guests a reason to move around. Best small party catering in Dubai is usually the simplest version, not the most elaborate one.

add_block.new_heading: Event catering menu ideas that actually work in a Dubai room
new_paragraphs: Here are event catering menu ideas by format, taken from menus myCHEF has run rather than from a template. Pick one line as the spine of the evening and build outward from it.

Finger food catering, Dubai corporate style. Finger food is what a standing room needs: one filling on one base, eaten in a single bite with a drink in the other hand. Kibbeh balls stuffed with hummus, halloumi dippers with pesto, mini shawarma wraps, vine-leaf shooters, beef sliders, tomato and basil crostini, prawn skewers, and a sweet tray of mini kunafa and date bites. Twelve pieces per variety is the practical minimum, and six to ten pieces per guest replaces a meal.

Grazing table. Mezze-led and built to be looked at: hummus, moutabel, muhammara and labneh, cheese and zaatar manakish, falafel, halloumi, olives, dried fruit and warm breads, with cheese and charcuterie at one end. It scales from 25 guests upward and needs no service staff once it is set.

Buffet for a mixed guest list. Five or six cold mezze, three hot mezze, one charcoal-grill section, two mains — a rice-and-meat centrepiece such as chicken mandi or lamb kabsa alongside a vegetarian main — and two desserts. Halal by default, with the vegan and gluten-free items sitting on the main line rather than on a separate table.

Live stations. A shawarma or mixed-grill station outdoors in the cooler months, a pasta or wok pan indoors, a saj or manakish station for a daytime event, and a kunafa or loukoumades station late on. One station per fifty guests keeps the queue moving.

Plated, chef on site. Three to five courses timed to the run of the evening: a canapé on arrival, a starter, a fish or vegetable course, a centrepiece main carved or plated, then dessert with coffee. This is the format that needs a chef in the room and prices at AED 700–950 per person.

new_paragraphs: How much does event catering cost in Dubai?

From AED 120 per person for a standard event buffet, AED 150 for premium buffet, BBQ, live stations or canapés, and AED 700–950 per person with a chef cooking and serving on site. Ready-made packages run AED 1,200 to 5,500, and a chef's tasting is AED 1,400.
What's included in event catering?
Included is menu design, a vetted chef, service staff where needed, all setup and full cleanup. Larger events add a bar team, styling and live stations.
How do I hire event catering in Dubai?
Share your date, guest count and venue; we send an itemised proposal, usually within one business day, then confirm a chef matched to your menu.
Do you cater corporate events, parties and weddings?
Yes — the same team handles corporate events, private parties and weddings, adapting the format from a plated gala dinner to a relaxed villa celebration.
Can you handle dietary requirements and halal menus?
Yes — menus are halal by default, with vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free and nut-free tracks mapped across your guest list before the day.
Where in Dubai do you provide event catering?
Across all of Dubai, from Palm Jumeirah and Emirates Hills villas to Downtown, the Marina, DIFC and desert venues, with the team and equipment travelling to you.
How far in advance should I book an events caterer in Dubai?

About 72 hours for a standard catering package, 3 to 5 days once live stations or multiple staff are involved, and 7 to 14 days for a wedding or a large corporate function. Short-notice requests are assessed individually against partner availability.
What is the cheapest way to cater an event?

Drop-off, because you pay for food and packaging and nothing else. It starts at AED 90 per person in Dubai with a 10-guest minimum and an AED 900 minimum order. A buffet from AED 120 is the next step up and adds presentation and a small team.
What is the minimum number of guests for event catering?

Ten guests for drop-off, platters and working-lunch formats, and twenty for a buffet, with a minimum order value of AED 900. A private chef cooking plated at your table has no minimum headcount, so a dinner for six is a real booking.
Do you do finger food catering in Dubai?

Yes. Finger food and canapés are priced from AED 150 per person as a premium volume format, built as one filling on one base — kibbeh balls, halloumi dippers, mini shawarma wraps, sliders, prawn skewers and sweet bites. Count six to ten pieces per guest to replace a meal.
For event catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .
